Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Senegal has a fully deployed nationwide biometric national ID system. The ECOWAS National Biometric Identity Card (ENBIC/CEDEAO card) has been issued since 2016 — Senegal was the first ECOWAS country to do so. The Directorate of File Automation (DAF) under the Ministry of Interior manages the biometric population register and issues national ID cards, passports, and residency documents. As of 2025 approximately 10 million citizens (>90% of adults aged 15+) hold a biometric card. A new digital identity layer (INN – Identifiant Numérique National) was launched in 2022 with UNDP support as part of the Digital Senegal 2025 strategy. The 2025 'New Deal Technologique' targets a unique biometric digital ID for all sectoral uses by 2034.
